claims.text: Applying a protective surface coating by a deposition technique will improve the surface physical and mechanical characteristics of components in aggressive environments.
A thin, conformal DLC coating can be deposited on the component surfaces using PACVD.
The DLC coating will remain effective during exposure to corrosive chemicals.
The DLC coating will remain effective under high mechanical stresses.
The DLC coating will remain effective at variable temperatures up to approximately 400°C, provided its stability limits are not exceeded.
The DLC coating acts as a robust physical barrier.
The DLC coating fills surface micro-defects.
The DLC coating distributes mechanical loads across the surface.
The DLC coating passivates the substrate against chemical attack.
Depositing the DLC layer enhances surface hardness.
Depositing the DLC layer enhances wear resistance.
The DLC layer reduces material degradation by minimizing surface abrasion.
The DLC layer reduces material degradation by inhibiting corrosive reactions with the substrate.
DLC-coated components will exhibit at least a 20–30% increase in hardness relative to untreated components under simulated aggressive conditions.
DLC-coated components will exhibit reduced abrasion or wear rates relative to untreated components under simulated aggressive conditions.
The surface-property improvement will persist as long as temperature, load, and corrosive exposure do not compromise the coating's integrity.

contradictions.description: The predicted hardness increase is at least 20–30%, but the falsification rule requires only a 15% improvement. A result between 15% and 20% would fail to achieve the stated prediction while not falsifying the hypothesis.
